newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 10.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on January 10:

WASHINGTON - The House ethics committee chairman abruptly postponed next week's public hearings in the case of House Speaker Newt Gingrich after Democrats complained about what information lawmakers would have before voting on punishing the speaker.
WASHINGTON - D.C. Mayor Marion Barry's administration issued a plan that would eliminate 2,411 goverment jobs as part of citywide reductions to meet 1997 budget targets.
WASHINGTON - A small commuter plane slammed into a field about 18 miles southwest of Detroit while preparing to land in deteriorating weather, killing 29 people.
WASHINGTON - The mysterious murder of six-year-old JonBenet Ramsey in Colorado puts child beauty pageants in the spotlight.

WASHINGTON - The 332-page report documenting an alleged right-wing media "conspiracy" to publish negative stories about President Clinton was compiled by a young aide toiling in an obscure corner of the White House.
MOSCOW - Russian capitalists wield vast influence in a country where ideology was once the source of power. ---

WASHINGTON - Montgomery County's decision to open schools on schedule despite a snowstorm and then close early, angered many parents who were forced to make hasty arrangements to pick up their children.
